A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Long-LRM. All main-text and appendix pages are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and retained content can be matched across the substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on DL3DV-140 and Tanks and Temples, architecture and loss ablations, and qualitative results in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds refinement, RealEstate10K, 2D Gaussian and ScanNetv2 results, including additional appendix ablations.

M1.justification: v2 Section 4.1 introduces optional post-prediction optimization of Gaussian positions and colors using input-view rendering loss. It also adapts Long-LRM to predict 2D Gaussians through additional fine-tuning. These extend the reconstruction procedure and output representation, while the original hybrid architecture, token merging and regularization losses remain.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained DL3DV and Tanks and Temples evaluations, v2 adds two-view novel-view synthesis on RealEstate10K and zero-shot ScanNetv2 evaluation of image rendering, depth maps and reconstructed meshes. This substantially expands both dataset coverage and evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Mip-Splatting and Scaffold-GS alongside the retained 3D GS baseline. New comparisons include pixelSplat, MVSplat and GS-LRM on RealEstate10K, and optimization-based 2D GS on DL3DV and ScanNetv2. Appendix Table 9 additionally contextualizes depth results against COLMAP, Atlas and VoRTX under explicitly different input and supervision conditions.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a two-view 256-by-256 evaluation, additional 2D GS fine-tuning, and three- or ten-step refinement budgets. ScanNetv2 adds aspect-ratio augmentation, every-80th-frame image evaluation, depth evaluation across keyframes, and mesh construction using every-10th-camera depth maps with 4 cm TSDF voxels. The original main evaluation split and K-means input selection are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds constant-width token-merging controls in Table 4, merging-position ablations in Table 5, RealEstate10K loss ablations in Table 10, and transformer/Mamba ordering experiments in Table 11. These examine separate effects of token width, merging location, regularization applicability and training stability. The original loss and Gaussian-usage analyses remain as Tables 6 and 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The expanded results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises the reported 32-view DL3DV PSNR from 23.86 to 24.10 and time from 1.3 seconds to 1 second, and adds 25.60 PSNR after ten refinement steps. Numerous new benchmark and geometry results appear. The four-view final-model ablation changes from 21.25 to 20.43 PSNR, and its parameter count from 162M to 142M. These revisions are not fully explained and do not establish a controlled performance improvement.

T1.justification: The state-space equations, complexity statements, token-merging mathematics and original loss definitions are retained, with notation and equation-numbering changes. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion expand the contributions to include compatibility with 2D GS and geometry reconstruction, while the conclusion adds superiority over previous feed-forward methods in sparse-view settings. The claimed reconstruction latency changes from 1.3 seconds to 1 second. The central claim of instant wide-coverage reconstruction remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of damage from naive opacity pruning, depth supervision encouraging spherical-harmonic color representation instead of translucent floaters, reduced need for regularizers with two-view inputs, and stability from distributing transformer blocks. It replaces v1's speculative explanation of the LPIPS gap with an explanation of reduced floaters through learned priors and regularization. The 64-view scaling and field-of-view limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds Gaussian color degree, scale and opacity biases, expanded camera-normalization instructions, refinement learning rates and frozen parameters, and geometry-evaluation implementation details. These substantially expand reproducibility information. However, it omits v1's explicit first-7K-training-scenes disclosure and near-plane settings, including the different setting used without depth supervision; their omission does not establish that those settings changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused positioning against object-level Gamba/MVGamba and city-scale Gaussian optimization methods. References also expand to support the new baselines, 2D GS adaptation and datasets. The existing related-work framework and central positioning of hybrid, wide-coverage reconstruction remain.

P1.justification: The six-section progression and much of the method and training exposition remain. v2 tightens prose and captions, swaps the dataset and implementation subsections, introduces result subheadings, and reorganizes the appendices. Citation style, affiliation text and acknowledgements also change; much of the additional prose documents new scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from single-column to two-column layout, rearranges Figure 1, expands Figure 3 with additional comparators, and adds color/depth and RealEstate10K figures. Tables are expanded and newly arranged, including compact side-by-side displays. v1's appendix Figure 4 survives as v2 Figure 6, and the original loss and usage tables are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence by replacing a narrow main comparison with several relevant alternatives, adding direct sparse-view comparisons, and separating token-merging effects from token-width choices through additional ablations. ScanNetv2 image, depth and mesh evaluations also provide concrete support for the geometry extension. These gains outweigh the loss of training-subset and near-plane disclosures and the unexplained ablation-score revisions, although those reporting issues reduce reproducibility and confidence in exact numerical comparisons.
